issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Ride.abbreviation as type char (problem_statement.md: UML Ride shows -abbreviation: char). In the solution, Ride declares abbreviation as a String (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java: line with 'private String abbreviation;' and constructor 'public Ride(String name, String abbreviation)'). However, several other solution classes (RollerCoaster, LaunchedRollerCoaster, LaunchedDropdownTower) use char for the abbreviation parameter in their constructors (e.g. solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java constructor signature uses 'char abbreviation'). This creates an inconsistent type usage across the solution: the Ride class expects a String while subclasses/constructors expect a char. The mismatch will confuse students about the correct type to implement (char vs String) and causes compilation/implementation problems (superclass constructor signature does not match subclass constructor calls).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the abbreviation type consistent across the specification and code. Recommended: align the solution with the UML/problem statement by changing Ride.abbreviation to type char (private char abbreviation;), update the Ride constructor to accept a char for abbreviation, and change the getter to return char. Ensure all subclasses and constructors use the same char type when delegating to the superclass. Alternatively, if the intended design is to use String abbreviations, update the UML/problem statement and tasks to specify String instead of char.
